# Privacy Policy

What we collect, why, and what you can do about it.
Effective October 25, 2026 · See also [Terms of Service](../terms/)

## 1. Who we are
Regretamin (regretamin.com) shows founders information about venture capital, private equity and hedge fund firms from public sources. It is operated by **Know Your Group INC.**, a Delaware corporation ("we", "us"), which is responsible for the personal data described here. Questions or requests: **malytskyyo@gmail.com**.

This policy covers two groups of people: **users** of the site (sections 2–7) and **people named on firm pages** (section 8).

## 2. What we collect from users
- **Account.** Your email address, or, if you sign in with Google, the name, email address and profile picture Google shares with us. Used to create and secure your account.
- **Saved firms.** The firms you save and the firms you have unlocked, so you can find them again under My firms.
- **Credits.** Your credit balance and a record of each credit used or added (which firm, when).
- **Firm requests.** If you search for a firm we don't have yet, the name you typed and, if you give it, your email so we can tell you when it's ready.
- **Submissions.** If you send us information about a firm, we collect what you send, any evidence (such as documents or emails, including proof of your relationship with the firm), your contact details, and the date. See section 7.
- **Correction requests.** Your message, contact details and any documents you send.
- **Payment records.** Stripe handles payments; we never see or store card numbers. We keep your Stripe customer and subscription IDs, your plan and its renewal date.
- **Abuse prevention.** When a free credit is used, or information is submitted, we store a one-way hash of your IP address (not the address itself).

## 3. Free searches and your device
Without an account you get 2 free credits on your device. To count them, your browser stores a random ID in its local storage (`regretamin.anon`), and our database keeps the count against that ID. It does not contain your name or email. A new account gets its own 4 credits. Device credits are not transferred. Signing in also stores a session token in your browser, and starting a purchase stores a short-lived note of the plan you picked. Clearing your browser storage removes all of these.

We don't use advertising cookies, ad trackers or analytics tools.

## 4. How we use user data
- To run the service: sign-in, credits, unlocking firms, saved firms and purchases.
- To send sign-in links and, if you asked, an email when a firm you requested is ready.
- To review, verify and publish submissions, and to handle correction requests and replies.
- To keep the service secure and prevent abuse.
- To keep records we need to comply with the law and to defend legal claims.

We don't sell your personal data, don't share it for advertising, and don't show ads.

## 5. Services we use
- **Supabase:** our database and sign-in (accounts, credits, saved firms). Sign-in link emails are sent through Supabase.
- **Stripe:** payments, subscriptions and promo codes.
- **Google:** only if you choose Google sign-in. Our pages also load fonts from Google Fonts, which receives your IP address.
- **Resend:** sends the email telling you a firm you requested is ready.
- **GitHub Pages:** hosts the website. Page code also loads from the jsDelivr content network.

These providers process data on our behalf under their own terms. Most are in the United States, so your data may be processed outside your country. Where required, we rely on the transfer safeguards these providers offer (such as Standard Contractual Clauses or the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework).

## 6. Legal requests
We may keep and disclose information when we must respond to valid legal process (such as a court order or subpoena), to protect our rights, or to defend legal claims. We share with authorities only when the law requires it.

## 7. Information you submit about firms
- **Your identity stays private.** We don't publish your name or contact details unless you agree. We may have to disclose them if a court or law requires it.
- **Verification.** We use your evidence to check the information. We publish a submission only after verifying it against an independent source (which we then cite), or as a clearly labeled, attributed unconfirmed report with a named public source.
- **Anonymity is not guaranteed.** Details you include can sometimes identify you, even if we never publish your name.
- **Subpoenas and court orders.** We disclose a contributor's identity only in response to a valid subpoena or court order in an active lawsuit. Where the law allows, we will try to tell you first (using the email you gave us) so you can object or get legal help. We may choose to oppose requests we believe are improper, but we can't promise we will or that we'll succeed.
- **Retention.** We keep submissions, evidence and our review notes for up to 6 years so we can show where information came from and defend legal claims, unless the law requires otherwise.

## 8. People named on firm pages
If you are a partner, executive, limited partner or other person connected with a firm, we may show limited information about you.

- **What we show:** your name, role, and firm affiliation, and what public records and published sources say about you, such as court and regulatory records, sanctions listings and press coverage. Unconfirmed reports are shown only with a named public source, attributed to it, and labeled "Not confirmed by official records."
- **Sources:** court dockets, SEC EDGAR and IAPD, OFAC and other government sanctions lists, company registries, published press, and verified user submissions. Each entry shows its source and the date we last checked it.
- **What we don't show:** home addresses, personal phone numbers or email, family details, ID numbers, or your nationality or ethnicity. The one exception is when nationality is part of an official listing, such as a sanctions designation. We never present nationality, on its own, as a sign of wrongdoing.
- **Sanctions matches:** a "possible name match" means only that a name looks like one on an official list. We keep it labeled that way unless the official listing confirms it.
- **Why:** to help founders understand who they take money from, a matter of public interest. Where the EU or UK GDPR applies, our legal basis is legitimate interests (Article 6(1)(f)), which we have balanced against your rights, together with applicable freedom-of-expression exemptions. Information about legal proceedings is shown only as it appears in official or published records.
- **Your choices:** you can ask to access, correct or delete information about you, object to its use, or add a reply, free, at malytskyyo@gmail.com. We will respond within 30 days. We correct or remove what is inaccurate and remove items shown to be false. For accurate information, we weigh your request against the public interest in accurate information about investors. **We never charge to change or remove information.**

## 9. How long we keep it
- Account data, saved firms and credit records: while your account exists.
- Payment records: longer where tax or accounting law requires.
- Submissions, correction requests, and the source copies and edit history behind each firm page: up to 6 years, to show where information came from and to defend legal claims.
- Hosting providers keep their own logs for their own periods.

## 10. Your rights
You can ask us to access, correct, export or delete your data, or to stop using it, by emailing malytskyyo@gmail.com. We may need to confirm it's you, and we won't treat you differently for asking.

Depending on where you live (for example the EU, UK, California or other U.S. states), you may have more rights, including complaining to your local data protection authority. **California and other U.S. states:** we do not sell or share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising, about users or people named on firm pages.

## 11. Children
Regretamin is not for anyone under 18, and we don't knowingly collect data from children. If you believe a child has an account, contact us and we'll delete it.

## 12. Security
Data is encrypted in transit and access to our database is restricted. No system is perfectly secure.

## 13. Changes
If we change this policy, we'll update the date above. For significant changes we'll also tell people on the site.

## 14. Contact
Know Your Group INC. · malytskyyo@gmail.com

This policy is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without limiting any rights you have under the law where you live.

# Terms of Service

The rules for using Regretamin, in plain English.
Effective October 25, 2026 · See also [Privacy Policy](../privacy/)

## 1. Agreement
These terms are an agreement between you and **Know Your Group INC.**, a Delaware corporation that operates Regretamin at regretamin.com ("we", "us"). By using the site you accept these terms and our Privacy Policy. You must be at least 18.

## 2. What the site is, and is not
Regretamin helps founders and their advisers learn about venture capital, private equity and hedge fund firms before taking their money.

- **It is not legal, investment or financial advice.** Do your own diligence before you take or turn down money.
- **It gives no verdicts.** We don't rate firms or people as good or bad.
- **It is not a consumer reporting agency.** Know Your Group INC. is not a "consumer reporting agency," and Regretamin does not provide "consumer reports," under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. §1681 et seq.) or similar laws. You must not use Regretamin to decide anyone's eligibility for credit, insurance, employment, housing, or any other purpose covered by those laws.

## 3. Where our information comes from
We compile information from public sources: court dockets, government and regulatory databases (such as SEC EDGAR and IAPD, and the OFAC and other government sanctions lists), company registries, and published press. Where clearly marked, we also show unconfirmed reports from public sources (section 5) and information submitted by users (section 6).

Each entry shows its source and the date we last checked it. We report what those sources say. We do not independently confirm every underlying allegation, and an entry reflects its source as of the date shown. Records can be incomplete, out of date or wrong.

## 4. No findings of wrongdoing
A lawsuit, complaint, regulatory filing, news article, report or list entry is not proof that anyone did anything wrong. Allegations in lawsuits are only allegations; many are dismissed or settled with no admission. We describe court and government records as what they are (for example, "according to a complaint filed in [court] on [date]") and show the outcome when we know it.

Labels such as "flag" or "check" describe the type of public record under our published methodology (see "How we check"). They are not statements about anyone's character or conduct, and they are not recommendations to take or refuse an investment.

## 5. Unconfirmed reports
Some entries are reports found publicly online that are not official records, for example press stories, published interviews, or public posts. We show an unconfirmed report only when:

- it links to a **named public source** that anyone can check;
- it is **attributed** to that source ("According to [source], …"), not stated by us as fact;
- it is **clearly labeled "Not confirmed by official records"**; and
- it is dated.

We do not publish anonymous gossip, rumors without a public source, or private information. Showing a report means only that the source said it. It does not mean we believe or endorse it. The firm or person named can reply (section 9), and we remove any item shown to be false.

## 6. Sanctions and watchlist data
Sanctions entries come from official government lists (such as the U.S. Treasury OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List, the EU Consolidated List and the UK sanctions list) and from services that collect those lists. We show each entry with its official source and listing date.

- A **confirmed match** means the official listing identifies that person or entity.
- A **possible name match** means a name (and any identifiers shown) looks like a listed party. It does **not** mean they are the listed party.
- **Nationality, citizenship, residence or place of business is never, on its own, a sign of sanctions status or wrongdoing**, and we don't present it as one.

Always check the official list before you rely on a sanctions entry.

## 7. Submitting information
You may send us information about a firm or the people connected to it. By submitting, you confirm that:

- it is true, accurate and not misleading to the best of your knowledge;
- you have personal knowledge of it, or you give us a source for it;
- when we ask, you will give supporting evidence, which can include proof that you have or had a relationship with the firm (for example, a term sheet, emails, or proof you are a founder it invested in or spoke with);
- you have the right to share it, and sharing it doesn't break a confidentiality agreement or the law; and
- you are not submitting it to harass, retaliate against, or compete with anyone.

We may verify, edit for accuracy, label, decline or remove any submission. We publish a submission only after we verify it against an independent source (and then we cite that source), or as a clearly labeled, attributed unconfirmed report under section 5. We don't publish your name unless you agree. You keep ownership of what you submit and give us a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, verify, display and keep it to run Regretamin.

## 7a. Content standards for submissions
Submissions must be about a firm's conduct as an investor and must not:
- accuse anyone of a crime, fraud or sanctions violation unless an official record or named public source says so (cite it);
- state as fact something you know is false or misleading, or present rumor as fact;
- include private personal information (home addresses, personal phone numbers or emails, family members, health, ID numbers) or anyone's nationality or ethnicity as a criticism;
- disclose information you are bound by contract or law to keep confidential; or
- be submitted by someone with a conflict of interest (for example a competitor, or a current employee of the firm) without saying so.

We may decide in our discretion whether a submission meets these standards. Reviewing, editing for accuracy, labeling, declining or removing submissions is an editorial choice that does not make us the author of user-provided information.

## 7b. Anonymity of contributors
We try to keep contributors' identities private, but we cannot guarantee anonymity: details in a submission can sometimes identify the person who sent it. Please consider that before you submit. You may expose yourself to legal liability if your submission is false or breaks the law.

## 8. Credits
1 firm = 1 credit. Using a credit unlocks one firm's full page. Reopening a firm you already unlocked is free. Without an account you get 2 free credits on your device; creating a free account adds 4 more. We may change free amounts with notice on the site. A single credit costs {{plan.single.price}}. Credits have no cash value and can't be transferred.

## 9. Corrections and replies
Anyone named on Regretamin, including firms, partners and limited partners, can ask for a correction, add context, or send a response, free, at **malytskyyo@gmail.com** (or our corrections form when available). Tell us the page and entry, what is wrong, and include any supporting documents.

- We acknowledge requests within 5 business days and aim to resolve them within 30 days.
- If an entry is inaccurate, we correct or remove it. If it is accurate but incomplete (for example, a case was dismissed), we update it.
- On request, we may publish a short factual reply from the named party next to the entry.
- **We never charge to change or remove information, and no one can pay us to add, keep or remove an entry.**

## 9a. Reporting content
Every entry has a "Report" link (or email malytskyyo@gmail.com). Once notified, we review the entry against these terms and its source. Flagged entries stay visible while we review, unless they appear to break the law or reveal private information. We do not remove accurate, sourced information just because a firm or person disagrees with it, and paying customers get no say in what is shown about others.

## 10. Subscriptions and promo codes
Plans: {{plan.starter.name}} is {{plan.starter.price}}/month for {{plan.starter.checks}} credits a month, or {{plan.starter.yearly.price}}/year. {{plan.pro.name}} is {{plan.pro.price}}/month for {{plan.pro.checks}} credits a month, or {{plan.pro.yearly.price}}/year. Prices are shown before you pay. Stripe handles payments, subscriptions and promo codes.

A subscription renews automatically until you cancel. Plan credits refill each month, and unused plan credits don't carry over. You can cancel any time from your Account page; your plan stays active until the end of the paid period. Promo codes apply only as described when you enter them, can't be exchanged for cash, and may expire or be withdrawn. If you think you were charged in error, email us and we'll look at it. This doesn't limit any refund rights you have under law.

## 11. Acceptable use
Don't:

- scrape or bulk-download the site, or use bots;
- get around credit limits (for example with many accounts or by resetting device storage);
- interfere with the service or access other people's accounts;
- resell or republish our pages without permission; or
- show Regretamin information without its source, date and labels, or in a way that changes its meaning.

## 12. Accounts and termination
Sign in with Google or an email link. You are responsible for activity on your account. You can stop using the site at any time and ask us to delete your account. We may suspend or close accounts that break these terms.

## 13. Our content and links
The site design and the way we compile and present information belong to us. You may share links and quote short excerpts with attribution. Underlying public records belong to their sources. We link to sources we don't control and aren't responsible for their content or availability.

## 14. Matters of public concern
Regretamin publishes information on matters of public concern: who funds companies, and the public legal and regulatory record of investors. We will defend that publication, including under applicable anti-SLAPP laws such as Delaware's Uniform Public Expression Protection Act (10 Del. C. §6001 et seq.).

## 15. Disclaimers and liability
**REGRETAMIN IS PROVIDED "AS IS" AND "AS AVAILABLE." TO THE EXTENT THE LAW ALLOWS, WE DISCLAIM ALL WARRANTIES, INCLUDING ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS AND FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. WE ARE NOT LIABLE FOR ERRORS OR OMISSIONS IN GOVERNMENT OR THIRD-PARTY SOURCES, FOR INDIRECT OR CONSEQUENTIAL LOSSES, OR FOR DECISIONS YOU MAKE BASED ON THE SITE, INCLUDING DECISIONS TO ACCEPT OR DECLINE AN INVESTMENT. OUR TOTAL LIABILITY FOR ANY CLAIM IS LIMITED TO THE GREATER OF USD 100 OR WHAT YOU PAID US IN THE 12 MONTHS BEFORE THE CLAIM.** Some places don't allow these limits, so they may not apply to you.

## 16. Indemnity
You agree to defend, indemnify and hold harmless Know Your Group INC. and its officers, employees and agents from claims, losses and costs (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising from information you submit, your breach of these terms, or your misuse of the site.

## 17. Disputes

**Arbitration and class waiver.** If we can't resolve it, any dispute between you and us about Regretamin or these terms will be settled by binding individual arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Consumer Arbitration Rules, not in court. Either of us may instead bring an individual claim in small claims court. **You and we each give up the right to a jury trial and to take part in a class or representative action.** You can opt out of this arbitration section by emailing us within 30 days of first accepting these terms. header._note: Firm header labels (js/company.js). The hero card row is not drawn. The HQ city stays in the meta line. SEC facts with an SEC source stay as linked pills. Regulatory AUM and Fund gross assets are different figures. A stored Assets or AUM label that is not a gross-asset figure reads as Regulatory AUM. Average check is the label on the stages pill line when firm.check_size is set. The amount is the formatted US dollar bounds. The stored source sentence is not the pill. No value: no label and no divider.

social._note: Social pills under the meta line: follower count only, accounts linked from the firm's own website (firm_page.firm.social). No data: no row.

videos._note: Videos section under Team. Up to 3 YouTube interviews, most views first. Grey line is channel, date, and view count. No source pill. No rows: no section.

checking._note: Checking view on /vc/<slug>/ while a firm's 10 checks are not all done (js/company.js summary + js/app.js). {firm}, {done}, {check}, {when}, {email} are filled in. started is the Pacific date and time from RegretDate.
